findings.highlight: the fatigue of the training is finally hitting my body
findings.evidenceJa: 日中の鍛錬の負債が、ここにきて一気に圧し掛かってきた
findings.governingReading: The accumulated debt from daytime training suddenly bears down on Shirou all at once.
findings.explanation: The English removes the debt metaphor and weakens the abrupt accumulated burden to fatigue finally arriving.

findings.highlight: My mind must be more tired than my body
findings.evidenceJa: 体より精神がまいっているのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether his mind is more exhausted than his body.
findings.explanation: The English promotes his question into a confident conclusion.

findings.highlight: I want to pass out right here in the hallway
findings.evidenceJa: 廊下で眠ってしまいたい
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels as if he wants to fall asleep in the hallway.
findings.explanation: The English replaces sleep with involuntary loss of consciousness.

findings.highlight: sleeping in her room
findings.evidenceJa: 客間で眠っている
findings.governingReading: Shirou corrects himself that Sakura should still be asleep in the guest room.
findings.explanation: The English again makes the borrowed guest room sound like Sakura’s own room.

findings.highlight: from Rider not taking form
findings.evidenceJa: ライダーを使役してない分
findings.governingReading: Illya attributes Sakura’s apparent improvement to not employing or commanding Rider.
findings.explanation: The English shifts agency from Sakura not using her Servant to Rider independently not materializing.

findings.highlight: those empty houses
findings.evidenceJa: あの空虚な廃墟
findings.governingReading: The consumed district appears as empty ruins.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the work-wide ruined landscape to individual empty houses.

findings.highlight: I can still lay out the futon in my current state
findings.evidenceJa: 満足に働かない頭でも布団だけはきちんと敷ける
findings.governingReading: Daily habit lets Shirou properly lay out the futon even though his mind is not functioning adequately.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the specific cognitive impairment with vague “current state” and omits the precision of the habitual action.

findings.highlight: gives me enough composure to make me think
findings.evidenceJa: 少しだけ考える隙間が出来た
findings.governingReading: Lying down creates a small opening or mental space in which Shirou can think.
findings.explanation: The English changes limited cognitive room into sufficient emotional composure.

findings.highlight: the day ended in a flash
findings.evidenceJa: 簡単に終わっていた
findings.governingReading: The supervised exposure seemed to have ended with disturbing ease.
findings.explanation: The English changes ease into speed and makes the whole day, rather than the session, the thing that ended.

findings.highlight: She is losing her freedom with each passing day
findings.evidenceJa: 日に日に自由がきかなくなっている桜
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s body is increasingly ceasing to obey or move freely each day.
findings.explanation: The English turns failing bodily control into abstract loss of freedom.

findings.highlight: the crest worm is sucking the magical energy from her
findings.evidenceJa: 刻印虫に体を蝕まれ、魔力が足りない
findings.governingReading: The Crest Worms are eroding Sakura’s body and leaving her short of magical energy.
findings.explanation: The English retains energy consumption but omits the physical erosion of her body.

findings.highlight: I’ve already made my choice
findings.evidenceJa: とうの昔に決めている
findings.governingReading: Shirou says the choice was settled long ago.
findings.explanation: The English removes the long duration of his prior commitment.

findings.highlight: I came since I heard sounds
findings.evidenceJa: 物音がしたものだから起きてきちゃいました
findings.governingReading: Sakura says the noise woke her and brought her out of bed.
findings.explanation: The English mentions hearing sounds but omits that they woke her.

findings.highlight: doesn’t say what she wants, is at a loss
findings.evidenceJa: 言いたい事をいつも我慢して損をして
findings.governingReading: Sakura habitually suppresses what she wants to say and suffers for it.
findings.explanation: The English mistranslates suffering loss or disadvantage as being verbally or mentally at a loss.

findings.highlight: still smiles at me
findings.evidenceJa: 一生懸命に笑おうとする俺の大事な女の子
findings.governingReading: She is Shirou’s precious girl, still striving with all her might to smile.
findings.explanation: The English removes the effort and invents Shirou as the direction of the smile.

findings.highlight: I can sleep well tonight
findings.evidenceJa: 今夜はよく眠れそう
findings.governingReading: Sakura says it seems she will be able to sleep well tonight.
findings.explanation: The English promotes her hopeful appearance into certainty.

findings.highlight: She can’t be different
findings.evidenceJa: いつも通りじゃない桜なんてあってたまるものか
findings.governingReading: Shirou defensively refuses to permit the possibility of a Sakura unlike herself.
findings.explanation: The English turns his emotional insistence into a factual claim that she cannot differ.

findings.highlight: Were you sleeping like I told you?
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと眠ってたか
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether Sakura slept properly.
findings.explanation: The English invents a prior instruction as part of the question.

findings.highlight: Yes. I’m very happy.
findings.evidenceJa: いえ。すごく、嬉しいです
findings.governingReading: Sakura answers “No” to Shirou’s question whether she dislikes the embrace, then says she is very happy.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the response polarity, creating a contradiction with her happiness.

findings.highlight: I just wanted to do this with Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: ただ、桜とこうしていたかった
findings.governingReading: Shirou simply wants to remain together with Sakura in this state.
findings.explanation: The English makes the referent an ambiguous act rather than continued closeness.

findings.highlight: I wanted to hold Sakura many times
findings.evidenceJa: 何度も桜を抱きしめたかった
findings.governingReading: Shirou wants to embrace Sakura over and over until consciousness breaks.
findings.explanation: The English produces unnatural count-based phrasing for repeated embraces.

findings.highlight: It’s Sakura that needs to be satisfied
findings.evidenceJa: 求めている、欲しているのは桜の方
findings.governingReading: Sakura is the one actively seeking and desiring Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English removes Sakura’s agency and adds a passive need for satisfaction.

findings.highlight: I want it more than her
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の方が、桜以上に満ち足りずにいる
findings.governingReading: Shirou finds himself even less fulfilled or satisfied than Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English changes an emotional state of unfulfillment into comparative desire for an undefined act.

findings.highlight: I feel Sakura’s warmth on my hand
findings.evidenceJa: 掌に桜の体温を感じながら
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels Sakura’s body heat through his palm while holding her hand.
findings.explanation: The English relocates embodied warmth to the surface of his hand and drops the bodily-temperature specificity.

findings.highlight: I fall asleep
findings.evidenceJa: 深い眠りに落ちた
findings.governingReading: Shirou falls into deep sleep.
findings.explanation: The English omits the depth of his collapse into sleep.

findings.highlight: The haze clears from my mind
findings.evidenceJa: 昂ぶっていた頭は、眠りの淵で冷静さを取り戻す
findings.governingReading: At the brink of sleep, Shirou’s excited or aroused mind regains composure.
findings.explanation: The English replaces arousal, restored calm, and the threshold of sleep with generic clearing haze.

findings.highlight: by indulging in Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 桜に溺れる事で
findings.governingReading: The inward voice accuses Shirou of losing or drowning himself in Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the self-erasure metaphor with morally and sexually loaded indulgence.

findings.highlight: finally confirm a certain unease
findings.evidenceJa: 決定的に、ある不安を認めてしまった
findings.governingReading: Shirou may have decisively and unwillingly admitted a particular fear.
findings.explanation: The English changes self-admission into evidentiary confirmation and temporalizes decisiveness as “finally.”
